chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The obligatory and supererogatory prayers are fifty-one rakʿahs. Of them are two rakʿahs after al-ʿatamah, performed sitting, which are counted as one rakʿah while standing. The obligatory prayers among them are seventeen rakʿahs, and the supererogatory prayers are thirty-four rakʿahs.

key_terms.أَرْبَعٌ وَ ثَلَاثُونَ: the number of supererogatory rakʿahs in the daily cycle
key_terms.النَّافِلَةُ: the supererogatory prayer units performed in addition to the obligatory prayers
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: the night prayer time, referring here to after the ʿIsha prayer
key_terms.اَلْفَرِيضَةُ: the obligatory prayer units that are legally required
key_terms.سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ: the number of obligatory rakʿahs in the daily prayers

ai.seo_question: How many total daily obligatory and supererogatory rakʿahs are there in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the total number of daily obligatory and supererogatory rakʿahs as fifty-one. It clarifies that the two rakʿahs offered after al-ʿatamah while sitting are counted as one standing rakʿah, with the obligatory prayers totaling seventeen and the nawafil totaling thirty-four.
